title: FloodGuard Private Flood Policy — Cancellation Conditions
content:
Policy conditions of the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy on cancellation at the named insured's request and cancellation for nonpayment.

## A. Cancellation at the named insured's request

A.1 A FloodGuard policy is cancelled at the named insured's request only for an accepted cancellation reason, on a request the named insured has signed. The named insured's signed request states an accepted cancellation reason; this is judged on the cancellation request on file — its stated reason and its outcome — for that request.

A.2 The accepted cancellation reasons and the basis of each are:

| Accepted reason | Credit basis |
|---|---|
| The property was sold | Pro rata |
| Duplicate coverage | Pro rata |
| The loan was paid off | Pro rata |
| The building was destroyed, not by flood | Pro rata |
| The loan never closed | Flat |

A.3 A request for any other reason, including that the lender no longer requires flood insurance, is declined midterm; the named insured may instead choose not to renew.

A.4 The cancellation takes effect on the date of the reason — the sale closing date, the other policy's effective date, the payoff date, the date the building was destroyed — but never before the effective date and never more than 30 days before the date the signed request is received.

A.5 A policy that is still bound, before coverage attaches, may be cancelled on the named insured's signed request, for example because the loan never closed.

**Boundary cases for A.4 (hypothetical dates).** A signed request is received on 20 June. A sale closing date of 21 May lies 30 days before receipt and is within the limit; a sale closing date of 20 May lies 31 days before receipt, more than the 30 days allowed, so the cancellation cannot take effect on that date. A payoff date that falls before the policy's effective date cannot be the cancellation date either.

## B. Retired clauses — no longer in force

B.1 The former clause under which the credit followed the reason's basis — pro rata being the term premium multiplied by the calendar days from the cancellation date to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent; flat returning the whole term premium; and the policy fee never being returned — is **no longer in force**.

B.2 The former clause under which, when a claim has been paid in the term and the tier makes the term premium fully earned once a claim is paid, the premium is fully earned and no credit is posted, is **no longer in force**.

Both have been superseded by the current basis for the cancellation credit.

## C. Cancellation for nonpayment of the second two-pay installment

C.1 A nonpayment notice for the second two-pay installment is issued once it is still unpaid more than the tier's nonpayment notice days after its due date. The notice places the policy in pending cancellation and is copied to the mortgagee.

C.2 The cancellation is scheduled the tier's nonpayment cancellation notice days later, and never sooner than the tier's mortgagee notice period when a mortgagee is on file.

C.3 The notice is rescinded only by payment of the amount due before the scheduled cancellation date; the policy then returns to in force. When the scheduled date arrives without payment, the policy is cancelled.

C.4 A nonpayment cancellation credits pro rata.

**Worked timeline (hypothetical, periods of 15, 10 and 45 days as on every FloodGuard tier).** The second installment is due on 1 March. On 16 March it is 15 days past due, not more, so no notice issues; on 17 March it is more than 15 days past due and a notice may issue. A notice issued on 17 March schedules the cancellation 10 days later, on 27 March, where no mortgagee is on file; with a mortgagee on file the cancellation is scheduled no sooner than 45 days after the notice, on 1 May. Payment of the amount due on 30 April rescinds the notice; no payment by 1 May leaves the policy cancelled on that date.

superseded_clauses: The credit follows the reason's basis: pro_rata is term_premium multiplied by the calendar days from the cancellation date to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent; flat returns the whole term premium; and the policy fee is never returned.
When a claim has been paid in the term and claim_paid_fully_earned is true, the premium is fully earned and no credit is posted.
